industry: B2B Distribution / Industrial MRO & Fasteners Distributor
businessModel: Regional business-to-business distributor of maintenance-repair-operations (MRO) supplies, fasteners, fluid-power, and safety products serving manufacturers, contractors, and municipalities through outside sales reps, branches, and a growing e-commerce storefront
businessStage: Mature, family-owned third-generation distributor under margin pressure from digital price transparency
sourceNote: Real-world pattern from regional industrial-distribution consolidation and the digital disruption of B2B MRO (mirrors public patterns from the Grainger/Fastenal/MSC competitive set and the rise of Amazon Business price transparency). Reflects the well-documented distributor margin-leak problem: thousands of SKUs priced via legacy cost-plus matrices and rep discretion, where undisciplined discounting, stale price files, and 'me-too' matching against transparent online prices erode gross margin even as revenue holds. Metrics reflect typical industrial-distribution economics (gross margin %, SKU count, customer/SKU price-band dispersion, rep-override rates).

ownerIntake.businessType: Third-generation family-owned industrial MRO and fastener distributor, founded 1971. 6 branches in two states, 240 employees, 22 outside sales reps, ~52,000 active SKUs. ~$96M revenue TTM. Sells to ~3,100 active business accounts (manufacturers, mechanical/electrical contractors, municipalities). E-commerce storefront launched 2 years ago now ~14% of revenue and growing.
ownerIntake.stage: Revenue $96M TTM, roughly flat (+1.5% YoY). Blended gross margin fell from 27.4% to 24.1% over 24 months (-330bps) while operating expenses held flat as a percent of sales, so operating margin dropped from 6.1% to 3.2%. Inventory turns 4.1x (industry top-quartile 5.5x+). Rep-discretion price overrides occur on ~38% of order lines. Price files for ~60% of SKUs not updated against vendor cost increases in over 9 months.
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: Recover blended gross margin to 26.5%+ and operating margin to 5%+ within 12 months without losing more than 2% of revenue, to fund a planned warehouse-automation investment and a possible third-generation ownership transition.
ownerConstraints: Gross margin fell 330bps in 24 months while revenue stayed flat; the leak is in margin, not volume.
22 outside reps have broad pricing discretion and override list prices on ~38% of order lines, frequently matching customer-cited online/competitor prices with no margin floor.
~60% of SKU price files have not been updated against vendor cost increases in 9+ months, so pass-through of cost inflation is incomplete and inconsistent.
E-commerce (14% of revenue) exposes the catalog to direct price comparison with Amazon Business, Grainger, and Fastenal, increasing customer price sensitivity on commodity SKUs.
Reps are compensated on revenue, not margin; sales culture resists any change perceived as 'taking away their ability to win deals.'

No segmented pricing strategy exists: commodity, A-brand, and proprietary/low-competition SKUs are all priced on the same legacy cost-plus matrix, leaving margin on the table on differentiated products and over-discounting commodities.
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: Operating margin has halved (6.1% to 3.2%) over 24 months even though revenue is flat, driven almost entirely by a 330bps blended gross-margin decline. Leadership cannot tell whether the erosion is from incomplete cost pass-through (stale price files), undisciplined rep discounting, unfavorable customer/product mix shift toward low-margin commodities, or competitive price matching forced by e-commerce transparency. With a warehouse-automation investment and an ownership transition both depending on restored margin, leadership must identify the dominant leak before changing pricing, rep comp, or the e-commerce strategy.

ownerIntake.riskAppetite: MEDIUM-LOW (margin recovery cannot come at the cost of losing key accounts or triggering a rep exodus; a clumsy across-the-board price hike could drive volume to transparent online competitors)

businessProblem: A mature family-owned industrial MRO distributor has seen blended gross margin fall 330bps (27.4% to 24.1%) over 24 months on flat revenue, halving operating margin (6.1% to 3.2%), with the leak driven by some combination of stale price files (~60% of SKUs not cost-adjusted in 9+ months), undisciplined rep discounting (overrides on ~38% of order lines, reps paid on revenue), unfavorable mix shift toward commodities, and competitive price matching forced by e-commerce transparency (now 14% of revenue). Management must determine which of these is the dominant margin leak before changing pricing strategy, rep compensation, or e-commerce approach — because an undifferentiated across-the-board price increase risks driving volume to transparent online competitors and a rep-comp overhaul risks a sales-team exodus, while inaction stalls a warehouse-automation investment and an ownership transition both contingent on restored margin.

evidence.finding: Blended gross margin fell from 27.4% to 24.1% (-330bps) over 24 months while revenue stayed roughly flat (+1.5%) and operating expenses held flat as a percent of sales — so operating margin dropped from 6.1% to 3.2%. The deterioration is entirely a margin (price-versus-cost) phenomenon, not a volume or cost-structure problem: the same revenue is yielding far less gross profit per dollar.
evidence.source: Financial statements, gross-margin trend, opex ratio analysis

evidence.finding: Pricing governance is broken: ~60% of the 52,000 SKU price files have not been updated against vendor cost increases in 9+ months, so cost inflation is being absorbed rather than passed through, and reps override list price on ~38% of order lines with no margin floor. There is a single legacy cost-plus matrix applied uniformly across commodity, A-brand, and proprietary SKUs, with no segmentation by competitive intensity or pricing power.
evidence.source: ERP price-file audit, order-line override report, pricing-process review

evidence.finding: E-commerce has grown to ~14% of revenue and exposes the catalog to direct price comparison with Amazon Business, Grainger, and Fastenal, increasing customer price sensitivity specifically on commodity SKUs. However, a large share of the 52,000-SKU catalog is differentiated, application-specific, or proprietary, where pricing power remains — the distributor is not distinguishing between the two when it discounts or matches.
evidence.source: E-commerce channel data, competitive catalog comparison, SKU-category review

supportingData.price_sensitivity: High on commodity SKUs, lower on proprietary
supportingData.catalog_mix: Mix of commodity and differentiated/proprietary SKUs

evidence.finding: Reps are compensated on revenue, not margin, and sales culture resists changes seen as limiting their ability to win deals. Inventory turns at 4.1x versus a top-quartile 5.5x+, indicating working capital tied up in slow SKUs, but this is a secondary efficiency issue distinct from the gross-margin leak. No data yet confirms whether the 38% override rate reflects genuine competitive necessity or reflexive discounting of deals that would close at list.
evidence.source: Compensation plan review, inventory turn analysis, sales-culture assessment
